note_to_future_researcher: IMPORTANT MISFILE DISCOVERY, logged 2026-08-21. This file was handed to the wargaming-researcher agent as 'the Block War supplement' for the Warlord Games 2020 Judge Dredd Miniatures Game (see meta.json in this folder). It is NOT that. Read this before doing anything else with block-war.pdf.
what_it_actually_is: The Judge Dredd Miniatures Game, published by Mongoose Publishing, approx. 2009-2013 -- a distinct, earlier, unrelated ruleset that happens to share the Judge Dredd IP license and a similar product name. This file is that game's 'Block War' expansion booklet (partial/living document per its own text: 'This is not the full Block War supplement. We will be continually adding more material... over the next few months!').
evidence: Copyright page (PDF page 2): 'Judge Dredd (TM) (c)2013 Rebellion Developments Ltd... www.mongoosepublishing.com... Revised 16th April 2013.'
Writer credited: Matthew Sprange (a Mongoose Publishing staff writer/designer, not Dylan Owen who wrote the Warlord 2020 book).

Core terminology throughout: Credits (force-building currency, '500 credits' starting budget), Rep (a Mordheim/Necromunda-style '1 + Hero Levels' reputation-and-rating stat), Minions and Heroes (hero/henchmen structure), Experience Points, Level 1/2/3 Heroes, Talents (58 hits) -- none of which appear anywhere in the Warlord 2020 rulebook.

Zero hits for 'Notoriety' as the Warlord book uses it (2 stray hits, unrelated usage), zero hits for 'Action chip', zero hits for '[HIT]/[ARMOUR]/[SPECIAL]' Combat dice faces, zero hits for d20/percentile either -- confirms an entirely separate core resolution engine that this supplement alone can't fully characterise (its own core rulebook was not present in the library folder to cross-check).
why_the_confusion_is_understandable: G:\My Drive\Wargaming\Judge dredd\ has a 'Judge Dredd (Mongoose)' folder, but it holds only Mongoose's separate 2d20/RPG line (Corebook, We Are The Law, etc.) -- not this miniatures game. Mongoose evidently published BOTH a Judge Dredd RPG line AND a separate, apparently lesser-known Judge Dredd Miniatures Game circa 2009-2013, and only this game's Block War supplement ended up filed alongside the Warlord 2020 miniatures game, with no core rulebook alongside it.
worth_a_future_capture: Partial skim (not a full read) turned up one genuinely interesting item for Settlements' territory/settlement-layer open question: a Territory-control campaign layer where a force earns discrete 'Territories' (rolled on a 2D6 table, each with a flat Credit income + a unique special ability, e.g. a Medtech Clinic lets you ignore one arrest per fight, a Ruined Block gives a free item worth <=25 credits after every fight but has a 1-in-6 chance per use of permanently running dry) capped at 10 held but gated to a smaller number 'managed' (income-generating) by a headcount-scaled table (2 or fewer force members manage 4 Territories, up to 15+ members managing all 10). This is a real, citable precedent for a territory-cap-by-crew-size mechanic if Settlements ever wants one, but it was NOT verified in depth, NOT cross-checked against a second reading, and belongs to a different, uncaptured game. Do not cite this as evaluated Judge Dredd Miniatures Game (Warlord) content. If pursued, it should get its own slug (e.g. judge-dredd-mongoose-minis) and its own vault note once the missing core rulebook is located, since 'one source, one note' applies and this is a different source from a different publisher.
recommendation: Leave uncaptured for this run. Flagged on the hub's to-read list as its own entry, not folded into the Judge Dredd Miniatures Game note.
